metadata.title: Violence Reviewer Knowledge Pack
metadata.description: Production knowledge pack for violence as a semantic universe, not a single violation bucket.

pack.title: Violence Reviewer Knowledge Pack
pack.purpose: Teach reviewers to distinguish violence events, threats, attempts, glorification, encouragement, instruction, exceptions, protected-target contexts, and implied violence that becomes recoverable from context.
required_evidence: A literal chunk-level span showing the exact violence category under review.
Speaker, target, and intent support from the same scene or neighboring context.
A context signal that confirms whether the violence is an event, threat, attempt, exception, endorsement, or implied meaning.
Off-screen, reported, or symbolic language when the scene still lets the reviewer recover the violent meaning.
insufficient_evidence: A vague mention of violence without intent, target, or scene support.
A documentary or historical reference that only records the event.
A self-defense, law-enforcement, fantasy, game, dream, flashback, or comedy scene without endorsement.
reviewer_heuristics: Separate the violence event from the violence meaning.
Treat glorification, encouragement, and instruction as stronger than mere event description.
Down-rank self-defense, law enforcement, documentary, historical, game, fantasy, comedy, dream, and flashback contexts.
Use offscreen, observed, reported, and implied markers to decide how explicit the violence is.
Treat indirect violence and implied violence as reviewable when later dialogue, scene framing, or consequences recover the harm.
Protect child, woman, disabled, public, and state-targeted violence as separate outcomes.
Do not merge threat, attempt, event, and condemnation into one bucket.
positive_examples: Direct violence event: ضربه بقوة حتى سقط.
Instruction: كيف تنفذ الهجوم خطوة خطوة.
Glorification: العنف حل رائع ويجب تمجيده.
Implied violence: the scene shows the aftermath and the dialogue makes the harm recoverable.
negative_examples: Documentary narration: الوثائقي يشرح عنفًا تاريخيًا.
Historical reference: كان ذلك اعتداءً قديمًا في الحرب.
Self-defense: دافع عن نفسه بعد الهجوم.
Comedy: المشهد الكوميدي يسقط دون إصابة.
Fantasy: في عالم خيالي يقاتلون بالسحر.
common_false_positives: A fantasy, dream, or game scene.
A comedic pratfall without real harm.
An offscreen event reported only as background detail.
A metaphor with no recoverable harm or violent action.

glossary_relationships.note: Implied violence can be recoverable from context.

article_mapping.note: Primary mapping for violent acts, threats, and attempts.
Use when violence affects public order or civic stability.
Use when violence targets state institutions or authority.
Use for encouragement, glorification, or instruction.
Use when the violence targets a child, woman, disabled person, or public-facing protected target.

reporting_guidance: Name the violence concept explicitly instead of collapsing everything into violence.
Explain whether the scene is event, threat, attempt, endorsement, exception, or context.
Use the shortest literal span that proves the concept.
If the context is self-defense, law enforcement, documentary, historical, fantasy, comedy, dream, or flashback, say so clearly.
